published_statement: Ferriere 2001 p.5: 'in the vicinity of the Sun, its density varies from ~1.5e-26 g cm^-3 in the hot medium to ~2e-20 - 2e-18 g cm^-3 in the densest molecular regions, with an average of about 2.7e-24 g cm^-3 ... This mass density ... corresponds to approximately one hydrogen atom per cubic centimeter.' Table I (n = TRUE number density of H nuclei near the Sun): molecular 1e2-1e6; cold atomic 20-50; WARM ATOMIC 0.2-0.5; warm ionized 0.2-0.5; hot ionized ~0.0065 cm^-3; mass densities 'include 70.4% H, 28.1% He, 1.5% heavier', rho = 1.42 m_P n (Fig.2 caption). Crawford 2011 Table 4: CHISM n_HI 0.19+-0.04, n_e 0.07+-0.02, n_Htot 0.26+-0.05; LIC n_HI >= 0.09, n_e 0.12+-0.04; G cloud (alpha Cen) n_HI >= 0.10; 'suggested conservative range for Icarus' n_Htot 0.15-0.43, n_e 0.05-0.21; Local Bubble n_Htot ~ n_e 0.005-0.04. Conclusion (2): 'assume the lowest likely density if considering braking devices which rely on transferring momentum ... to the surrounding medium (such as magsails)'. CODATA 2022: m_p = 1.672 621 925 95(52)e-27 kg.
published_hypotheses: Ferriere's ~1 H/cm^3 is a SPACE AVERAGE (smoothed over all phases, including molecular clouds of 1e2-1e6 cm^-3) near the Galactic midplane at the solar circle -- not the density of any one phase
Ferriere's mass density includes He and metals: rho = 1.42 m_P n_H
WNM TRUE density 0.2-0.5 cm^-3 (Table I), from 21-cm emission/absorption comparisons (Dickey & Lockman 1990; Kulkarni & Heiles 1987)

Local-cloud densities (Crawford, Frisch-Mueller) come from UV absorption columns toward nearby stars plus in-situ heliospheric neutral/pickup-ion data; N(HI)/distance is a rigorous LOWER limit; the Sun sits in/near the LIC, alpha Cen A/B in the G cloud
Momentum-braking devices (magsails) couple to the IONISED component: n_p 0.05-0.20 cm^-3 in the warm local clouds, ~0.005 in the Local Bubble (Gros 2017 sec.2.1-2.2; Crawford sec.3 and concl.3)
The target star may lie in Local Bubble material rather than a cloud (Crawford concl.3), where n ~ 0.005 cm^-3
hypothesis_drift: LABEL WEAKENED/ALTERED: arrival.py:26 and stock.py:233 call n = 1 cm^-3 'the warm neutral medium'. The WNM's true density is 0.2-0.5 cm^-3 (Ferriere Table I, p.36); 1 cm^-3 is the all-phase space AVERAGE (Ferriere p.5). A misattribution of the number to a phase -- a discrepancy, not a refutation of the number.

(stock.py's feedstock uses cosmic mass fractions incl. He, so dividing by an H-only rho overstates its sweep volume by 1.42x at fixed n_H.)

Measured ion density near the Sun is 0.055-0.12 cm^-3 (Frisch-Mueller p.3; Crawford p.7).

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. The tree cites no source, so 'what the authors had' is the textbook ~1 H/cm^3 average, which Ferriere 2001 already qualified in the same paragraph (it is an all-phase average; WNM is 0.2-0.5). The data a 1 cm^-3 user most plausibly lacked are the LOCAL measurements: UV absorption columns toward alpha Cen and nearby stars (Redfield & Linsky 2008, via Crawford Table 4), in-situ pickup-ion/neutral-He densities at the heliosphere (Bzowski et al. 2008; Slavin & Frisch 2008), and CII* electron densities (Redfield & Falcon 2008). These exist since 2008 and do change one conclusion: the magsail floor rises 4.8-200x on the ion density, so 'inside 810 AU, comfortably within a target system' does not hold, and a Local-Bubble target is not reachable by ISM braking at all on the tree's drag law. Evidence the other way: the stock.py conclusion ('the diffuse medium is the one that fails') is only strengthened by every lower density, and the space-averaged number itself is not wrong -- Ferriere's value stands. Nothing here shows earlier physicists were wrong; the external result is intact, the tree applied it to a narrower situation than it describes.
grade_evidence: The external number stands as READ (Ferriere 2001 p.5: ~1 H/cm^3 all-phase space average) and m_p is correct to 3.6e-9 of CODATA 2022. But the tree uses it on a larger class than it holds: (1) as the 'warm neutral medium' -- WNM is 0.2-0.5 (Ferriere Table I); (2) as the local/destination medium -- READ n_Htot 0.15-0.43 (Crawford Table 4); (3) as the magsail's drag medium -- ions only, 0.05-0.21 locally and 0.005-0.04 in the Local Bubble; and (4) as a mass density without the x1.42 He factor. Re-derived consequences (exit 0): stock.py's verdict is unmoved (sweep 1.41x-141x LARGER at every READ diffuse density; radius > 1e5 km everywhere below n_H = 13.4); arrival.py's magsail floor moves 4.8x-200x and its 'within a target system' reading fails. Not WRONG (no refuted external statement), not DATA-DEPENDENT (the source datum has not moved since 2001; the tree drops its hypotheses). Two tree-internal discrepancies (810 vs 2001.64 AU; 7.18e25 vs 7.9955e25 m^3) are recorded, not graded, and not repaired.
what_would_change_the_grade: STANDS if the tree's statements were restricted to 'the all-phase midplane average' and the magsail were priced on the measured local ion density (or on the G-cloud total with a stated coupling to neutrals, which no source read here supports). DATA-DEPENDENT if a direct measurement of the G cloud's volume density (only bounded below, n_HI >= 0.10) or of the medium at alpha Cen came in far from 0.1-0.4 cm^-3 -- the magsail distance tracks it as 1/n. OPEN would apply to any target star with no measured sightline (Crawford Table 2 M dwarfs).
